title: Pay changes from monthly to every two weeks mid-year: a monthly line covers the months each pay rule is in force, spread over that rule's pays; a change on a day other than the 1st leaves that month to the old rule (P4, R2)
story: Pay of 250,000 on the 25th (moved earlier) until a new job pays 110,000 every other Wednesday from Wed 10 Mar 2027 (the change starts that day). Set up Fri 26 Feb 2027, the day after the February pay: the bank holds 330,000; the opening split names nothing, so Food's share is by days left. Rent of 230,000 on the 1st. Food is 30,000 a month. Mon 1 Mar the rent is ticked. In 2027 the monthly rule is in force until 10 Mar: by R2 it covers January to March (3 months) with 2 pays (25 Jan, 25 Feb), so 90,000 over 2 pays. The two-week rule covers April to December (9 months) with its 22 pays from 10 Mar to 29 Dec: 270,000 over 22 pays, 12,272 each with 16 left over for the first 16. Every amount is made up.

asks.question: safe_to_spend
asks.why: 100,000 (bank today: 330,000 - 230,000 rent 1 Mar) - 41,538 (Food left this period: the period from pay@2027-02-25 gets 45,000, the monthly rule's 3 months over its 2 pays [P4, R2], x 12 of its 13 days left, rounded down [I4]) + 110,000 (pay 10 Mar) - 12,273 (Food for the period from 10 Mar: pay 1 of the two-week rule's 22, one of the first 16 that get a leftover unit) + 110,000 (pay 24 Mar) - 12,273 (Food for the period from 24 Mar, pay 2 of 22) - 230,000 (rent 1 Apr) = 23,916
asks.note: Spreading the whole year over all 24 pays of 2027 would give 15,000 a period; the plain form gives 30,000 (the first rule is monthly).
